text.div: The primary purpose of this trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of exoticillin in the treatment of bronchitis in Japanese patients with iatrogenic diabetes mellitus.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 2.1 Purpose of Trial

text.div: The main risk associated with the investigational intervention is the potential for hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, which has been observed in prior studies at a rate of approximately 1 in 10,000 patients.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 2.2.1.1 Risk Summary and Mitigation Strategy - Trial Intervention

text.div: Risks arising from trial procedures include discomfort and bruising from venepuncture, and a small risk of infection at injection sites during pharmacokinetic sampling visits.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 2.2.1.2 Risk Summary and Mitigation Strategy - Trial Procedures

text.div: There is a potential risk of disease progression in participants who do not respond to the investigational intervention. Rescue therapy protocols are in place to mitigate this risk.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 2.2.1.3 Risk Summary and Mitigation Strategy - Other

text.div: Exoticillin has demonstrated a clinically meaningful reduction in symptom duration in Phase II studies, with a mean reduction of 3.2 days compared to placebo. Benefits are anticipated to outweigh the identified risks in the target population.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 2.2.2 Benefit Summary

text.div: Based on the available non-clinical and clinical data, the benefit-risk balance for exoticillin in the treatment of bronchitis in Japanese patients with iatrogenic diabetes mellitus is considered favourable. The identified risks are manageable through the protocol-specified monitoring and mitigation measures.
